articles.title: How to insulate your home and stay warm during winter, according to experts
articles.summary: I spoke to multiple home experts to learn how to keep your home warm and insulated when the temperature drops, and the best hands-on tools to use.
articles.body: There are a lot of things to look forward to when the cold temperatures arrive: Refreshing your wardrobe with a new winter coat, sitting around a fire pit or taking a winter vacation. What isn’t as exciting is all of the home maintenance that comes with heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures. Aside from trying to clear your driveway with a snow blower or getting ice off your windows, your home may feel drafty or (worse) your pipes might freeze. This is why learning how to insulate your home is important. I spoke with home improvement, appliance and HVAC experts to learn more about different ways to insulate your home with affordable and accessible supplies available online, like tap and sealant. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for insulating your home in 2026 All of the products below are either recommendations from our experts or NBC Selected team of shopping experts, or have at least a four-star average rating from 500 or more shoppers on Amazon. One of the easiest (and most affordable) ways to help insulate your home is by using a draft guard, according to Lou Manfredini*, a home expert at Ace Hardware. Also called draft stoppers, door sweeps and draft snakes, these products are extremely straightforward: They block wind from creeping under your door and creating a draft throughout your home. With that said, there are a few different types of draft guards, such as this one from Grotheory, which has two long panels that attach to each side of your door. Each panel can cover up to a 1.5-inch gap between the floor and the bottom of the door. The panels are 39 inches long, but you can cut them to fit your door. You can put a panel on just one side or on both sides of the door, and installation takes only a few minutes, according to the brand. * Ace Hardware may earn revenue from any products recommended by Manfredini that are sold at Ace Hardware. This door sweep serves the same purpose as the GroTheory one mentioned above, but it has a different structure and form of installation. Instead of two panels that block each side of the bottom of the door, this door sweep has two foam padded blocks that fit around the sides of the door, and the bottom is a small flat panel that goes directly under it. It works for gaps that are between 0.5 to 1.7 inches. This type of draft guard is best for doors that don’t sit super high from the ground, but still let a substantial amount of wind or cold air inside. It fits door frames that are between 30 and 36 inches, according to the brand. Plus, each of the foam blocks has a cover that’s sealed with Velcro, so it doesn’t look like raw foam just hanging at the bottom of your door. Another way to insulate your home, whether you’re a homeowner or apartment dweller, is using blackout curtains, according to Dan Raysby, an HVAC manager at Abt Appliances and Electronics. “If you have a home that is older and has old windows, installing thermal curtains can make a big difference,” he says. “Installing throw rugs or carpeting insulates and helps keep the cold out as well.” These curtains aren’t only for blocking out light — they have thermal properties thanks to the way they’re woven and they have a sun-reflective coating that helps balance temperature indoors, according to the brand. And from a design and decor perspective, they loop on the back side to hide the rod. Another effective and easy way to insulate your home is by using a peelable and removable sealant (called weather stripping), which usually comes in a roll, similar to packing tape or a material similar in texture to caulk. Manfredini recommends applying weather stripping around windows and doors, as well as caulking the base trim to the floor to reduce drafts. You can apply this sealing tape around the edges of your window frame to prevent air from coming through. Similar to tape, you can cut it to the preferred length. This seal is also ideal for preventing drafts around window air conditioners, vents and door frames, according to the brand. While this may resemble a form of crown molding, it functions similarly to caulk or a piece of weather stripping tape. It’s a polyurethane material that comes in a roll and has a wedge shape that allows it to fit securely between cracks. It has an adhesive strip in the back to attach to a surface, like your window or door frame. You can also adjust the length and shape of the adhesive strip to help it fit more securely, such as around corners or edges. This caulk comes recommended by Manfredini* and functions in the same way as regular caulking that you might use to seal the edges around fixtures in your bathroom, except it is clear, removable and meant for window frames and vents. You apply it around the cracks on a window frame and allow it to dry for about 10 minutes. If you have to remove it, you can simply strip it away. Aside from drafts, it also helps block water and is suitable to use indoors and outdoors. * Ace Hardware may earn revenue from any products recommended by Manfredini that are sold at Ace Hardware. A separate option to try when insulating your home is a door frame cover, such as this one. The closures of the covers are filled with more than 50 magnets, so they seal closed securely. The covers are 38 by 82 inches (you can measure your door frame ahead of time, and if it’s slightly smaller, you can fold the hem to fit). It only requires three steps to install. All you have to do is clean the door frame and then attach the fastener to the frame. All of the supplies required to set it up are already included. It’s also pet friendly (dogs can get through easily without tearing it, according to the brand) and it prevents insects from coming inside. How I picked the best products for insulating your home There are a few important factors to keep in mind when choosing items to help insulate your home, especially if you plan on installing them yourself: Installation process: Before buying any gadgets, consider the limitations and infrastructure of your home. If you’re a homeowner, then you have a lot more liberty to make permanent changes. For example, you could have a professional install fiberglass in your attic, which heavily influences how your home maintains heat, according to Manfredini. If you rent, then you’ll have fewer options, though there are still several renter-friendly options to try. With this in mind, I made sure to include products that are suitable for both renters and homeowners.Reversibility: All of the products on this list are removable when the time comes to move out or simply uninstall during a different season. I also included items that are relatively easier to install regardless of skill level. How to shop for home insulation products Before buying a home insulation product, follow these steps to help you make the right decision. Consider your home type Depending on whether you’re renting or own your home, you may only be allowed to use certain types of products or complete certain renovations. For homeowners, the most important and effective place to start is the attic, according to Manfredini. If your home doesn’t have adequate insulation, “the heat you paid for is just leaving through the roof.” If you have a home with an attic, the most important thing to do is make sure it has a sufficient amount of fiberglass installed, which may be best done by a professional. If you don’t have an attic or aren’t a homeowner, Manfredini recommends trying a few easier-to-install (and remove) products such as window sealants or caulking, like the Xfasten Transparent Window Weather Sealing Tape and Dap Seal ‘N Peel Removable Caulk. Call a professional While many of the products above can make a huge difference in the overall warmth of your home, for a long-term and reliable solution, Raysby also recommends talking to a professional to look over your heating and cooling system. This includes your furnace, boiler, air conditioner and the fiberglass installed in your attic. articles.title: Moradores de Noronha visitam cemitério em obras no Dia de Finados | G1
articles.standfirst: O cemitério recebeu moradores que homenagearam familiares e amigos, apesar das obras que suspenderam os sepultamentos no local.
articles.summary: O cemitério recebeu moradores que homenagearam familiares e amigos, apesar das obras que suspenderam os sepultamentos no local.
articles.body:
Mesmo com as obras de ampliação do cemitério, moradores de Fernando de Noronha foram ao local nesta segunda-feira (2), Dia de Finados, para homenagear parentes e amigos que morreram ( veja vídeo acima ).

Como o espaço está em reforma, os sepultamentos estão suspensos e precisam ser realizados no continente até a conclusão dos trabalhos.

Moradores visitam o cemitério no Dia da Finados — Foto: Ana Clara Marinho/TV Globo

A aposentada Terezinha Lucas levou flores artesanais de papel, feitas por ela, para colocar no túmulo do marido, que morreu em 1998.

“Todos os anos eu venho. Sinto muita falta do meu marido. Acho muito importante colocar flores no túmulo dele no Dia de Finados”, contou.

A servidora pública Sandra Lima também foi ao cemitério para homenagear o pai e relembrar outros familiares.

“Meu pai morreu em setembro do ano passado e foi um dos últimos a ser enterrado aqui antes do início da obra. Nesse local também estão meu avô e meus primos. É um pouco da minha história. Venho sempre”, declarou.

O servidor público Ivan Lucas da Silva visitou o túmulo da esposa, que morreu há cinco anos.

“Esse é um dia de lembrar. Todos os anos eu venho. A saudade é muito grande”, disse.

Tereza visitou o túmulo do marido — Foto: Ana Clara Marinho/TV Globo

As obras de ampliação do cemitério começaram há mais de um ano e tinham previsão inicial de conclusão em seis meses. O g1 procurou a Administração de Fernando de Noronha para saber quando os trabalhos serão finalizados, mas não recebeu resposta até a publicação desta reportagem.

Segundo a Administração de Fernando de Noronha, a obra tem orçamento de R$ 2,67 milhões. O projeto inclui a ampliação da capacidade de sepultamento, a construção de uma capela, espaços para velórios, áreas de apoio, 132 gaveteiros e 60 ossuários. Também estão previstas pavimentação, estação de tratamento de efluentes e melhorias na estrutura.

articles.title: Filha de brasileiros era copilota de avião que caiu na Flórida | G1
articles.standfirst: Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, de 20 anos, ganhou destaque na imprensa americana em 2023, quando conquistou sua licença de piloto aos 17 anos. Jovem sonhava em trabalhar na aviação comercial.
articles.summary: Nathalia Filgueiras, de 20 anos, ganhou destaque na imprensa americana em 2023, quando conquistou sua licença de piloto aos 17 anos. Jovem sonhava em trabalhar na aviação comercial
articles.body:
Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, de 20 anos, filha de brasileiros, era copilota do avião particular que caiu no domingo (1º) em Palm Beach, na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos , matando as nove pessoas que estavam a bordo. A informação foi confirmada ao g1 por familiares da jovem.

A aeronave, um Learjet 60, havia decolado de Austin, no Texas, com destino às Bahamas. O avião caiu em uma área residencial e explodiu após atingir o solo. Todas as nove pessoas que estavam a bordo morreram, segundo o secretário de Transportes dos EUA, Sean Duffy.

Nathalia ganhou destaque na imprensa americana em 2023, quando conquistou sua licença de piloto particular aos 17 anos, antes mesmo de obter a habilitação para dirigir.

Nathalia Filgueiras aparece na cabine de um avião Learjet 60, em foto compartilhada nas redes sociais em março de 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Threads

Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, de 20 anos, era copilota do avião que caiu na Flórida e deixou nove mortos. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Na época, ela cursava o último ano do ensino médio na West Boca Raton High School, na Flórida, e foi entrevistada pela emissora americana CBS12 News sobre sua trajetória na aviação.

Segundo a reportagem, enquanto outros adolescentes de sua idade praticavam esportes ou aproveitavam os fins de semana com amigos, Nathalia dedicava boa parte do tempo a pilotar aviões.

“Eu até me gabo disso, porque as pessoas dizem: ‘Ah, você não sabe dirigir’, e eu respondo: ‘É, mas sei pilotar’”, contou à emissora.

O interesse pela aviação começou cedo. Segundo a reportagem, Nathalia iniciou seus estudos teóricos sobre pilotagem em 2020, quando estava prestes a entrar no segundo ano do ensino médio.

Ela também foi influenciada pelo pai, que havia começado a pilotar por lazer em 2018 e compartilhava seus conhecimentos sobre aviação com a filha.

A formação incluiu aulas teóricas, simuladores de voo, exercícios práticos e provas de conhecimentos técnicos. Em setembro de 2023, Nathalia conquistou sua licença de piloto particular.

Na época da entrevista, já havia acumulado 88 horas de voo e podia pilotar aeronaves particulares sozinha ou transportar passageiros, desde que não recebesse pagamento pelo serviço.

A formação foi custeada pelo distrito escolar de Palm Beach County, por meio de sua academia de aviação, que oferecia aulas e treinamentos a estudantes do ensino médio.

Em entrevista à CBS12 News, Nathalia contou que gostava de fazer algo diferente dos colegas e considerava mais interessante pilotar um avião do que dirigir um carro.

“Algumas pessoas acham estranho que eu consiga pilotar aviões, mas não saiba dirigir um carro. Acho engraçado e agora quero muito tirar minha carteira de motorista”, disse.

Na ocasião, ela tinha previsão de obter a habilitação para dirigir em novembro daquele ano.

🔎 Nos EUA, a idade mínima para obter uma licença de piloto particular é de 17 anos, segundo a Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA). Para isso, o candidato precisa cumprir os requisitos de treinamento, acumular pelo menos 40 horas de voo na modalidade regular de formação e ser aprovado em exames teóricos e práticos.

Já a licença de piloto comercial pode ser obtida a partir dos 18 anos e exige, em regra, pelo menos 250 horas de voo.

Para atuar como copilota de jatos executivos, também são necessárias habilitações e qualificações específicas, que variam conforme a aeronave e o tipo de operação.

Filha de brasileiros, a jovem começou a estudar aviação em 2020 e tinha o sonho de trabalhar como piloto de aviões comerciais ou jatos particulares. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Segundo Nathalia, seu objetivo profissional era se tornar piloto de uma companhia aérea comercial ou trabalhar na aviação executiva, pilotando jatos particulares.

Nas redes sociais, Nathalia também compartilhava momentos de sua rotina na aviação e comemorava conquistas profissionais.

Em uma publicação de março de 2026, a jovem apareceu na cabine de comando de uma aeronave, segurando um documento.

“Piloto em comando do Learjet 60! Toda a glória a Deus! Amém!”, escreveu na legenda.

Em publicação de março de 2026, Nathalia Filgueiras comemorou uma conquista como piloto em comando — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Nathalia Filgueiras aparece nos controles de uma aeronave durante voo, em imagem compartilhada nas redes sociais. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

A jovem iniciou seus estudos teóricos sobre pilotagem em 2020, quando estava prestes a entrar no segundo ano do ensino médio. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Um áudio da comunicação entre a tripulação e os controladores de tráfego aéreo registrou os momentos que antecederam a queda do avião.

Na gravação, uma voz feminina relata problemas com gelo e turbulência durante o voo. Pouco depois, a tripulante declara emergência e informa que o avião estava perdendo altitude rapidamente.

“Mayday, Mayday! Estamos descendo 10 mil pés por minuto”, diz a mulher.

🔎 O Mayday é uma chamada internacional de socorro utilizada em situações de emergência grave, quando uma aeronave precisa de assistência imediata.

Na sequência, a tripulante informa que o avião estava em uma condição de velocidade excessiva e perdia altitude a uma taxa de 20 mil pés (cerca de 6 km) por minuto.

Em seguida, uma das falas mais dramáticas da gravação: “Vamos bater no chão”. Em outro trecho, a mulher grita: “Olhe lá fora, Jack, olhe lá fora! Estamos sem tempo”.

Ainda não há confirmação de que a voz feminina registrada no áudio seja de Nathalia.

O Learjet 60 havia decolado de Austin, no Texas, às 9h36 do horário local (12h36 em Brasília), com destino às Bahamas.

O avião caiu às 12h50 (16h50 em Brasília), em uma área residencial de Greenacres, no condado de Palm Beach.

O impacto provocou uma explosão, abriu uma cratera no asfalto e espalhou destroços pela região.

As causas da queda ainda são investigadas pelo Conselho Nacional de Segurança nos Transportes dos Estados Unidos (NTSB), com apoio da Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA).

O NTSB realizará uma coletiva de imprensa nesta segunda-feira (2), às 15h (horário de Brasília), para apresentar informações sobre a investigação.

Segundo o NTSB, a coletiva abordará os procedimentos da investigação e as atividades previstas para os próximos dias no local do acidente.

Especialistas apontam que a formação de gelo e a turbulência podem ter contribuído para o acidente, mas ressaltam que ainda não há uma conclusão sobre o que provocou a queda.

articles.title: Corpo encontrado no Rio Amazonas em Macapá após desaparecimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima havia pulado de uma embarcação na tarde de domingo (1º). Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros trabalham na remoção e resgate do corpo.
articles.summary: O corpo encontrado no Rio Amazonas em Macapá é do homem que saltou de uma balsa no domingo para chegar à margem; Bombeiros e Polícia Científica atuam no resgate.
articles.body:
Corpo de homem que desapareceu no Rio Amazonas emerge na orla do Cidade Nova, em Macapá. — Foto: Josi Paixão/g1

O corpo do homem que estava desaparecido no Rio Amazonas desde o domingo (1º) emergiu no fim da tarde desta segunda-feira (2). A vítima foi avistada nas águas próximas à orla do bairro Cidade Nova, em Macapá .

Com o surgimento do corpo na superfície, os socorristas atuam no local para providenciar a remoção da água, segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Miltar do Amapá .

O homem desapareceu na tarde de domingo (1º) após saltar de uma embarcação que aguardava a subida da maré para conseguir atracar na orla da capital.

Segundo testemunhas, a vítima decidiu não esperar o desembarque e pulou na água com a intenção de chegar à margem nadando, acreditando que o trecho fosse raso. No entanto, durante o percurso, o homem não conseguiu prosseguir e afundou no rio.

O Corpo de Bombeiros iniciou as buscas com mergulhadores e embarcações no mesmo dia. Os trabalhos haviam sido suspensos ao anoitecer devido à visibilidade e retomados nesta segunda-feira (2).

A corporação reforça que o trecho da orla não é recomendado para banho por conta da força das correntes e da constante movimentação de embarcações.

articles.title: After Israel’s election: What’s next?
articles.summary: Knesset member Ofer Cassif argues that the ‘politics of exclusion’ keep Israel in political deadlock.
articles.body:
The success of Palestinian-led parties – who won 15% of the vote in Israel’s elections – has created a conundrum for Israel’s leadership: partner with non-Zionists or accept political gridlock. While the bloc led by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu got the most support from Israeli voters, it didn’t win enough seats in Israel’s parliament (Knesset) to build a ruling coalition so far.

Israeli politician Ofer Cassif, a member of one of the Palestinian-led parties, tells host Steve Clemons that the Israeli people “need to understand that the future must be a future of Jewish-Palestinian partnership and not another form of exclusion.”

articles.title: Suprema Corte rejeita tentativa do governo Trump de desconsiderar quase 20 mil votos da Califórnia | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo acumula derrotas judiciais em ofensiva para identificar possíveis eleitores sem cidadania americana antes das eleições legislativas.
articles.summary: Governo acumula derrotas judiciais em ofensiva para identificar possíveis eleitores sem cidadania americana antes das eleições legislativas.
articles.body:
Donald Trump — Foto: Jacquelyn Martin / AP

A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos rejeitou nesta segunda-feira (2) um pedido para que a Califórnia separasse milhares de votos enviados pelo correio por pessoas que, segundo o governo do presidente Donald Trump, não são cidadãos americanos.

A decisão ocorre na véspera das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato, consideradas decisivas.

A Suprema Corte se recusou a intervir em um caso envolvendo 20 mil pessoas identificadas pelo governo republicano como prováveis não cidadãos nas listas de eleitores da Califórnia, estado amplamente dominado pelo Partido Democrata.

Foi mais um episódio de uma série de disputas judiciais na véspera das eleições de meio de mandato, que definirão o controle do Congresso nos dois últimos anos do segundo mandato de Trump.

Na Califórnia, o governo Trump havia pedido à Suprema Corte que os votos contestados fossem separados até que a cidadania dos eleitores pudesse ser verificada.

Autoridades do estado, porém, afirmaram que a lista parecia conter muitos erros e que, na prática, a medida poderia impedir eleitores legalmente habilitados de votar.

A Suprema Corte não detalhou os motivos da decisão, como é comum em julgamentos de emergência.

Em setembro, os ministros já haviam rejeitado uma tentativa de Trump de restringir o voto pelo correio em todo o país , embora tenham decidido a favor de seu governo em uma série de outros recursos emergenciais.

Caixa do Serviço Postal dos EUA instalada em Manhattan, em Nova York — Foto: Andrew Kelly/Reuters

O governo republicano de Trump colocou como prioridade neste ano identificar eleitores que não sejam cidadãos americanos, apesar de esses casos serem raros.

Um juiz de primeira instância já havia rejeitado o pedido do Departamento de Justiça e alertado que a medida poderia impedir cidadãos de votar nas eleições de meio de mandato desta terça-feira, que definirão o controle do Congresso.

Também nesta segunda-feira, em Washington, outro juiz federal decidiu contra as tentativas do governo de impor exigências de última hora às autoridades eleitorais da Califórnia, concluindo que elas violavam a Constituição dos Estados Unidos.

“O Poder Executivo provavelmente violou a Cláusula Eleitoral da Constituição, que atribui a autoridade sobre as regras eleitorais exclusivamente aos estados e ao Congresso”, escreveu o juiz-chefe James Boasberg.

O governo afirmou que separar os votos era um pedido modesto e permitiria que os votos considerados legais fossem contabilizados posteriormente.

O governo sofreu uma sequência de derrotas nos tribunais nessa ofensiva e também foi criticado por esperar até poucas semanas antes da eleição para apresentar suas exigências às autoridades eleitorais da Califórnia, com base em uma lista que o próprio Departamento de Justiça admite não ser totalmente confiável.

Durante uma audiência para decidir se revogaria uma ordem que proibia o governo de ameaçar processar funcionários eleitorais que permitissem o voto de eleitores potencialmente inelegíveis, a juíza distrital Trina Thompson questionou detalhadamente os relatos de imprecisões generalizadas nos dados do Departamento de Justiça.

“Você concordaria que há uma alta taxa de erros?”, perguntou Thompson a Kenneth Kao, advogado do Departamento de Justiça. “É uma afirmação justa”, respondeu Kao. “É por isso que pedimos a ajuda dos responsáveis pelos registros eleitorais para verificar se todos eles são eleitores válidos.”

Ao mesmo tempo, Bill Essayli, procurador federal responsável pelo escritório do Departamento de Justiça em Los Angeles, afirmou em entrevista coletiva estar bastante confiante de que as pessoas da lista não tinham direito a votar.

“Isso não é especulação. Isso não é uma teoria”, disse Essayli, admitindo posteriormente que poderia haver erros na lista.

A votação está em andamento na Califórnia desde o início de outubro. Todos os cerca de 23 milhões de eleitores registrados no estado recebem uma cédula pelo correio, e centenas de milhares de votos já foram processados.

Autoridades eleitorais da Califórnia afirmaram que, neste momento, seria logisticamente impossível localizar e separar os votos contestados.

O procurador-geral da Califórnia, Rob Bonta, democrata, disse que o recurso "cheira a desespero e é mais uma tentativa de minar nossas eleições e atropelar o Estado de Direito".

Instâncias inferiores da Justiça deram razão ao estado. Um juiz distrital alertou que separar os votos provocaria "caos" nas eleições de meio de mandato e prejudicaria a confiança no processo democrático.

“Se o Executivo puder desconsiderar votos e ameaçar uma eleição em andamento com base em alegações não comprovadas, então nossa democracia estará em perigo”, escreveu o juiz federal David O. Carter, indicado ao cargo pelo presidente Bill Clinton, democrata.

Um painel de três juízes de um tribunal de apelações manteve a decisão por 2 votos a 1. Um juiz indicado por Trump e outro indicado pelo presidente Joe Biden, democrata, votaram pela manutenção da ordem. O terceiro integrante do painel, também indicado por Trump, discordou, argumentando que a recusa da Califórnia em separar os votos incentiva a "violação da lei federal".

O Departamento de Justiça tentou acelerar o andamento do caso e chegou a pedir, sem sucesso, a intervenção antecipada de um tribunal de apelações.

articles.title: Governo de Trump leva disputa eleitoral da Califórnia à Suprema Corte | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo Trump pede à Suprema Corte que impeça Califórnia de contar votos de mais de 20 mil eleitores suspeitos de não serem cidadãos americanos.
articles.summary: Governo Trump pede à Suprema Corte que impeça Califórnia de contar votos de mais de 20 mil eleitores suspeitos de não serem cidadãos americanos.
articles.body:
Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. — Foto: Nathan Howard/Reuters

O governo do presidente Donald Trump solicitou nesta segunda-feira (2) à Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos que impedisse temporariamente a Califórnia de contar os votos por correspondência de mais de 20 mil eleitores registrados que, segundo autoridades federais, provavelmente não são cidadãos americanos.

Em mais um capítulo da disputa judicial, que pode afetar milhares de eleitores nas eleições de meio de mandato desta terça-feira (3), o Departamento de Justiça pediu uma medida cautelar para suspender a contagem dos votos contestados até que a cidadania de cada eleitor seja verificada .

Um tribunal federal de apelações rejeitou o pedido na sexta-feira (30).

O governo americano intensificou as ações contra a suposta participação de não cidadãos nas eleições na reta final da campanha. Trump já fez alegações falsas sobre a existência de fraude eleitoral generalizada, inclusive na eleição de 2020, quando foi derrotado pelo democrata Joe Biden.

No entanto, diversos estudos e auditorias estaduais mostram que a votação irregular, inclusive por pessoas que não são cidadãs americanas, é rara.

A Constituição dos EUA atribui aos estados a responsabilidade de organizar as eleições, embora o governo federal exerça algum nível de supervisão.

A ação judicial representa uma rara intervenção federal no processo eleitoral e demonstra a disposição do governo Trump de contestar decisões relacionadas às eleições na Justiça.

O governo já havia tentado restringir o voto por correspondência — modalidade mais utilizada por eleitores com tendência democrata —, mas a Suprema Corte rejeitou a iniciativa em setembro.

A lista com os nomes de mais de 20 mil eleitores foi compilada pelo Departamento de Segurança Interna dos EUA e encaminhada às autoridades da Califórnia e do condado de Los Angeles.

Em 15 de outubro, o Departamento de Justiça entrou com uma ação na Justiça Federal, alegando que a Califórnia impede ilegalmente a aplicação de uma lei de 1996 que criminaliza o voto de não cidadãos em eleições federais.

Segundo o departamento, a conduta do estado viola a Cláusula de Supremacia da Constituição americana, que estabelece a prevalência da legislação federal sobre as leis estaduais em determinadas situações.

O governo pediu à Suprema Corte que determinasse à Califórnia a separação dos votos registrados por pessoas incluídas na lista e a suspensão de sua contagem até que a cidadania desses eleitores fosse comprovada.

"Uma vez que os votos ilegalmente emitidos sejam contados e misturados aos votos legítimos, o dano resultante é impossível de ser reparado", escreveu o Departamento de Justiça em um documento apresentado à Corte.

A Califórnia, por sua vez, afirmou que possui mecanismos rigorosos para impedir o voto de não cidadãos e que a ação do governo ameaça retirar o direito de voto de 20 mil pessoas com base em acusações vagas.

O estado também argumentou que o método utilizado pelo governo para identificar possíveis não cidadãos nos registros eleitorais é falho e provavelmente contém diversos erros, conforme documentos apresentados à Justiça.

articles.title: Chuva no Rio de Janeiro: Defesa Civil alerta para raios e ventos | G1
articles.standfirst: Há previsão de temporais na Região Metropolitana, Costa Verde, Sul Fluminense e Região Serrana. Calor aumenta nos próximos dias, antes da chegada de uma frente fria.
articles.summary: Com alerta de chuva no Rio de Janeiro e ventos fortes, a Defesa Civil orienta atenção; o calor chega a 36°C antes da frente fria derrubar as temperaturas.
articles.body:
Radar do Alerta Rio mostrava núcloes de chuva se aproximando da capital às 16h10 — Foto: Reprodução/Alerta Rio

Às 16h58 desta segunda-feira (2), a Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para pancadas de chuva e raios nas próximas horas na cidade do Rio de Janeiro. A orientação é evitar áreas alagadas.

Segundo o Alerta Rio, já havia registro de chuva moderada na Zona Oeste da capital por volta das 17h.

O aviso ocorre em um dia de sol e calor, com máxima de 34,6°C na capital, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).

De acordo com o Climaptempo, há previsão de temporais e rajadas de vento forte (em torno dos 80 km/h).

Na Costa Verde, no Sul Fluminense, na Região Serrana e na Região Metropolitana são esperados os maiores volumes de chuva.

Em caso de emergência, os moradores devem ligar para os números 199 ou 193.

⚠️ Recomendações da prefeitura em caso de chuva intensa:

Não tente atravessar áreas alagadas de carro, a pé ou de bicicleta. A água pode esconder buracos e objetos cortantes, além de oferecer riscos de correnteza e transmissão de doenças.

Evite ficar às margens de rios e córregos.

Ao dirigir, redobre a atenção e mantenha os faróis acesos.

Permaneça em local seguro e evite áreas sujeitas a alagamentos.

A terça-feira (3) também deve ter sol, calor e pancadas de chuva durante a tarde e o início da noite, principalmente no interior do estado. A chuva pode vir acompanhada de raios e rajadas de vento forte. Na capital, a máxima prevista é de 34°C.

O calor aumenta nos dias seguintes, com máximas de 35°C na quarta-feira (4) e de 36°C na quinta (5). Até lá, as pancadas de chuva devem ocorrer de forma isolada, à tarde e à noite.

Entre quinta e sexta-feira, uma frente fria passa pelo Rio e muda o tempo . A sexta-feira (6) deve ser nublada, com chuva fraca a moderada ao longo do dia. A máxima prevista cai para 26°C — dez graus abaixo da esperada para a véspera.

articles.title: Planejamento de carreira: como avaliar desempenho e crescer em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Período de balanço nas empresas pode ser aproveitado pelos trabalhadores para analisar resultados, identificar pontos de melhoria e estabelecer metas para a carreira em 2027.
articles.summary: Especialistas orientam como aproveitar o planejamento de carreira e a avaliação de desempenho no fim de ano para identificar metas e crescer no mercado em 2027.
articles.body:
Fim de ano é oportunidade para avaliar desempenho e planejar crescimento profissional, dizem especialistas — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/SVM

O fim do ano é um período de balanços e planejamento nas empresas. Enquanto gestores avaliam resultados e estabelecem metas para o próximo ciclo, os profissionais também podem aproveitar o momento para refletir sobre a própria trajetória e traçar objetivos para o desenvolvimento da carreira.

Em uma empresa do setor de siderurgia e metalurgia com cerca de 5,5 mil funcionários que recebeu a equipe da TV Verdes Mares, as reuniões de planejamento incluem a identificação dos colaboradores que se destacaram ao longo do ano. Raíssa Araújo, analista de Recursos Humanos, trabalha na companhia há quatro anos e explica que esse processo também ajuda a pensar nas oportunidades de desenvolvimento dos profissionais.

“A gente começa a pensar sobre isso, pensar no próximo ano”, afirma. Ela acrescenta que as discussões também consideram como os colaboradores podem se destacar no ano seguinte.

Para especialistas, esse período de planejamento das empresas pode servir de oportunidade para os trabalhadores avaliarem os próprios resultados e pensarem nos próximos passos profissionais . A mentora executiva de líderes Delania Santos recomenda uma análise sobre o desempenho e as contribuições de cada um ao longo do ano.

“Pensar nos resultados, pensar nas contribuições, ser protagonista da carreira dele”, orienta.

A coordenadora de Atendimento ao Cliente Dayane Carvalho, de 48 anos, procura manter esse planejamento como parte da própria trajetória profissional. Mineira, ela precisou construir os caminhos para chegar ao cargo de gestão, conciliando a rotina de trabalho com as responsabilidades de esposa e mãe.

Dayane conta que nunca deixou de estudar e buscou se preparar para aproveitar oportunidades profissionais.

“Em nenhum momento eu parei de estudar, né? Eu sou formada em duas faculdades, eu falo além do português e procuro estar preparada para qualquer oportunidade que aparecesse”, relata.

Para ela, a atualização constante é fundamental para acompanhar as mudanças do mercado de trabalho. “Se a gente não se atualiza, se a gente não se adapta, se a gente não tá um passo na frente, a gente não tá preparado”, afirma.

Como usar o planejamento da empresa a favor da carreira

De acordo com Delania Santos, as próprias movimentações da organização podem ajudar os funcionários a identificar caminhos para o desenvolvimento profissional. Reuniões, planos de expansão e novas metas da companhia, por exemplo, podem indicar quais competências serão valorizadas e quais oportunidades poderão surgir.

A mentora também destaca a importância de estabelecer objetivos de maneira intencional, com clareza sobre onde se deseja chegar e quais passos serão necessários para alcançar essa posição.

Para quem ainda não conseguiu uma promoção ou não alcançou o crescimento profissional esperado, a recomendação é evitar que a frustração com os resultados do ano impeça o planejamento do futuro. O momento pode ser usado para identificar aprendizados e pensar em mudanças de estratégia.

“Todo final de ano, as pessoas ficam com sentimento de nostalgia. Escolha fazer diferente”, aconselha Delania.

articles.title: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers
articles.summary: The home secretary laid out a revised proposal for changing when migrants can claim permanent residency.
articles.body:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has scrapped plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for permanent settlement.

Mahmood had proposed doubling the wait for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) from five years to 10 for most migrants, with some facing a 15-year wait.

But following a backlash from several Labour MPs, Mahmood revised the policy and care workers who earn at least £25,000 a year and arrived in the UK before May 2025 would continue to qualify after five years.

The Conservatives said Mahmood's "U-turn" would cost taxpayers billions of pounds.

ILR, also known as settlement, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible. They can also use it to apply for British citizenship.

Last November, Mahmood announced plans to delay settlements in response to concerns over the number of people approaching eligibility, in the wake of record post-Brexit net migration figures under the previous Conservative government, nicknamed the "Boriswave".

Asked by the BBC whether she had u-turned on her earlier promises, she replied "I don't accept that", adding that some 500,000 people in the UK "will not now settle at five years".

"They will have to wait longer before they can achieve settlement in this country, and I've come to a fair resolution for care workers," she said.

The Home Office has said its figures show net migration - the difference between those entering and leaving the country - added 2.6m people to the UK population between 2021 and 2024.

The department estimates that between 2026 and 2030 between 1.3m and 2.2m people will settle in the UK, adding its central estimate has increased to 1.9m.

The home secretary faced criticism for proposing to apply the changes to migrant workers already in the UK, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner previously saying this would "change the goalposts" .

Several Labour MPs also described the retrospective approach as "un-British" and warned it could worsen the UK's skills shortage, particularly in the care sector.

Making a statement to the House of Commons, Mahmood said settlement "should not be automatic, it should be earned".

Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

The changes will move those earning less than £50,000 a year onto a 10-year path to settlement status, unless they are exempt.

Mahmood also told MPs the government would provide a five-year path to settlement for care workers who "answered our call when we needed them" following the Covid-19 pandemic.

Mahmood said: "Those who earn £25,000 a year working in the social care sector, which was the condition of their visa, will therefore be able to settle on their existing five-year path."

She added those care workers who did not meet the conditions of their visa could apply for another five-year visa and seek settlement after that.

higher earners on salaries of more than £50,000 and those who have contributed in healthcare and education, such as doctors and teachers, will be able to qualify for settlement after five years

the highest rate taxpayers earning more than £125,000 will be able to apply after three years

refugees who arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they do not.

Mahmood said: "Our changes ensure those who are net contributors are encouraged to come to this country and stay here."

She added: "As a result, the Department for Work and Pensions estimates that our reforms will reduce the benefits bill by billions of pounds."

The original version of the plans announced by Mahmood last year would have delayed 799,000 people from gaining permanent residency. Under the updated plans announced on Monday, that number would drop to 517,000.

One of those affected was Ashfak Juned, a Bangladeshi chef working in Birmingham, who told the BBC he was "crying" when he heard his wait for settled status would now last until 2033.

The home secretary also confirmed a number of groups would see their settlement path remain as it is today - including Hong Kong British nationals overseas, armed forces members, people with a British connection and those on legacy routes including the Windrush scheme.

The Refugee Council's Imran Hussain said the plans for those who had travelled to the UK illegally or by small boat and do not work or study to wait 30 years for ILR were "unfair and unworkable".

"The fairest reforms would be making fast and good quality asylum decisions, with those refugees granted protection being helped to rebuild their lives and to contribute, and those with no right to remain helped to leave with dignity," he said.

For the Conservatives, shadow home secretary Chris Philp said opposition from Mahmood's fellow ministers and the "Labour open borders left" had resulted in the changes from Mahmood's original proposals, adding that she was "no longer running the government's immigration policy".

He highlighted figures from March in which Home Office calculations suggested 196,000 care workers and their adult dependants could settle between 2026 and 2030, at an estimated lifetime cost of £9.5bn to taxpayers.

Philp said this was the "cost of today's U-turn".

But Father of the House Sir Edward Leigh, the longest-serving male MP in the Commons, criticised his Conservative colleague for overseeing the so-called Boriswave after Brexit, where net migration peaked at nearly one million in 2023.

"Some of us don't have amnesia," he said.

Liberal Democrat home affairs spokesman Max Wilkinson said the government's reforms were "unravelling".

He added: "Viewing immigration simply as a matter of raw numbers and images of small boat arrivals is degrading this nation's ability to have the informed national discussion that we need."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Mahmood had "shown her true colours".

"She talked a big game on immigration but has u-turned at the first sign of trouble from her left wing Labour colleagues," he said.

Pointing to Home Office estimates that more than 200,000 immigrants arriving on Health and Care visas would be eligible for British citizenship before the next election, he claimed this would cost the taxpayer £50bn over their lifetimes.

He vowed to review citizenship of all those arriving on care visas from today and extend the qualifying period for citizenship to a minimum of 10 years.

Green Party MP Siân Berry said Mahmood had provided a "new obstacle course of hoops and barriers" for migrants living in the UK.

On Monday, the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank said that skilled workers and their dependants due to settle in the UK under current rules are expected to make a net lifetime contribution of around £115bn through the taxes they pay.

articles.title: 'Look outside, Jack!' Who was the man called out by female pilot Nathalia in final moments of Learjet crash?
articles.summary: The identity of the man addressed as “Jack” by pilot Nathalia Gadelha in the final moments of the fatal Learjet 60 crash in Florida remains unconfirmed,
articles.body: The identity of the man addressed as “Jack” by pilot Nathalia Gadelha in the final moments of the fatal Learjet 60 crash in Florida remains unconfirmed, even as the chilling cockpit recording has triggered speculation on social media. Many surmised that Jack was probably Nathalia's boyfriend with whom she used to fly frequently.In the audio circulating online, a female voice is heard shouting, “Look outside, Jack! Look outside!” before adding, “Holy f**k, we’re out of time.” The exchange came as the aircraft was rapidly losing altitude. However, neither investigators nor authorities have publicly identified the man addressed in the recording.Gadelha, 20, was identified as one of the pilots aboard the aircraft after her mother, Camila, confirmed to the New York Post that her daughter was co-piloting the jet. The Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County on November 1, killing all nine people on board. The aircraft had departed Austin, Texas, and was headed to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has confirmed the crash and said the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will lead the investigation.The mystery surrounding the crash intensified as the identity of the passengers has not been revealed yet.Who was Jack?Social media users have attempted to identify Jack by examining Gadelha’s online posts and personal life. One widely circulated post by an X user, Evan Kilgore, claimed that the letter “J” appeared in her Instagram bio and suggested that it could refer to her partner, whom the user believed was the man addressed in the recording.The post also claimed that Gadelha had regularly shared pictures of flying with him and that a male voice could be heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer during the emergency. These claims have fuelled speculation that Jack may have been her boyfriend or a person who regularly flew with her.A report by The Sun said Gadelha’s male co-pilot was heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer during the distress call, but added that he had not been identified.What happened in the final moments?The Learjet crew initially reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation to air traffic control. The situation then deteriorated rapidly, with the crew reporting that the aircraft was descending at 10,000 feet per minute before declaring an overspeed condition and reporting a descent of 20,000 feet per minute.Gadelha was heard warning, “We’re going to crash into the ground.” An air traffic controller responded, “I’m here with you. Talk to me.”The crew reported a descent of around 22,000 feet per minute. The recording then captured the words addressed to Jack, followed by the final warning that they were out of time.The FAA said the Learjet 60 crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, at around 12.50 pm local time on November 1. Nine people were on board. The aircraft had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. articles.title: Violence in northern Ethiopia pushing health system towards collapse: WHO
articles.summary: Renewed fighting between rebels from northern Tigray and the government in Addis Ababa has shattered 2022 peace deal.
articles.body:
Fighting and drone strikes in northern Ethiopia are pushing the country’s fragile health system towards collapse, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reported in a statement released on Monday that the conflict between rebels from the northern Tigray region and the government in Addis Ababa had killed several civilians in recent days and strained medical facilities.

“As fighting continues, more people are likely to lose access to essential healthcare, including emergency services, maternal and child healthcare and treatment for diseases,” he warned.

At least 15 people, several of them children, died in a series of drone strikes that hit a camp for displaced civilians in ⁠⁠Ethiopia’s Amhara region on Friday, sources involved in a rescue operation told the Reuters news agency.

Tedros, the world’s highest-profile Tigrayan, confirmed that children were among those reported to be killed at the Jaari 2 displacement camp in Amhara. In Rama, in neighbouring Tigray, several people were killed while seeking food.

Tedros gave no overall casualty tolls from the attacks and did not identify the perpetrators. However, he warned that drone attacks and civilian casualties were becoming more frequent across Ethiopia, worsening public health and humanitarian issues.

“The violence in northern Ethiopia is pushing an already fragile health system closer to collapse,” he said. “Hospitals face shortages of health workers, medicines and equipment. Ambulance services are severely limited. Insecurity is obstructing the delivery of life-saving medical supplies to some areas.”

The WHO and other United Nations agencies are working to deliver additional supplies, Tedros said. He called for civilians to be protected and for health workers and products to be allowed to reach those in need.

Renewed fighting between an alliance of rebels from the northern Tigray region and the government in Addis Ababa has all but shattered the November 2022 peace agreement between the two groups, stoking fears of a wider conflict.

articles.title: Nukes, Netanyahu, and November: Tucker Carlson raises nuclear war alarm for Nth time
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent From Washington: Somewhere in Washington DC, the nuclear clock is apparently ticking.
articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: Somewhere in Washington DC, the nuclear clock is apparently ticking. At least according to Tucker Carlson, a former Fox News host and penitent Trump loyalist, who says the U.S President may be hours away from ordering a nuclear strike on Iran under pressure from Benjamin Netanyahu. The target, according to Carlson, is Pickaxe Mountain, a heavily fortified underground complex near Iran's Natanz nuclear facility.“Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day,” Carlson quoted an “informed observer” as saying in a lengthy post on X, claiming that the Israeli PM is “cornered and desperate” after last week’s election results, and he can’t form a government unless Trump helps him. "The only military option is a nuclear strike," Carlson wrote, alleging that the Trump administration has quietly rewritten the U.S nuclear doctrine since February to make battlefield nuclear weapons easier to use.Carlson also dragged in India, Pakistan, and other nations into his alarmism. A U.S strike, he warned, would unleash radioactive contamination across the Persian Gulf, potentially trigger nuclear escalation involving Russia, India, Pakistan and North Korea, and bring about World War III."After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final,” he wrote, without explaining why others would get involved.Carlson has been sounding variations of this alarm for months, suggesting that even Armageddon has trouble keeping appointments. The latest post was greeted with ridicule in serious policy circles despite the adventurism of Trump and his MAGA cohorts. Indeed, there is a rather significant gap between the gravity of the claims and the evidence offered to substantiate it.Neither the White House nor the Pentagon has confirmed a change in nuclear doctrine. Carlson identifies no named American official, produces no documentary evidence and relies on anonymous sources for his central claims. Trump himself told Newsmax in October: "I wouldn't use nuclear. We don't have to."Still, U.S hardliners have been raising the prospect of an imminent nuclear confrontation with Iran for months, repeatedly drumming up the bogey of Tehran acquiring nuclear weapons within weeks or months. Carlson’s own interview in March with former National Counterterrorism Center director Joe Kent was revealing. Asked whether Iran had been on the verge of acquiring a nuclear weapon, Kent replied: "No, they weren't three weeks ago when this started, and they weren't in June either." He also said there was no intelligence indicating that Iran was about to abandon its policy against developing nuclear weapons.The American bogey of Iran getting nuclear weapons within weeks has now acquired a life of its own with one widely circulated meme features an ancient stone tablet supposedly dating to 1750 BC, bearing the inscription: "Iran is only weeks away from developing nuclear weapons." Another version has archaeologists discovering a 3,000-year-old tablet warning that Persia was weeks away from the bomb.Carlson is also accused of having his own agenda in cranking up the nuclear alarm. Once among Trump's most enthusiastic media champions, he has become one of the most consequential dissenting voices within the MAGA movement, and his break with Trump has been particularly pronounced over Israel and Iran.Carlson has argued that America should not subordinate its foreign policy to Israeli interests or be dragged into another Middle Eastern war. He has attacked Netanyahu's influence in Washington, questioned the rationale for American military intervention and challenged the longstanding assumption among Republican conservatives that supporting Israel is an unquestionable article of faith. The nickname "Qatarlson", popularised by his critics, including Laura Loomer and other pro-Israel conservatives, suggests that his criticism of Israel reflects Qatari influence rather than independent conviction.There are also larger ideological divisions at play here. One faction of MAGA believes America First means resisting foreign entanglements, particularly wars undertaken for Israel; another regards unwavering support for Israel as integral to U.S national security and conservative politics. Carlson has become a lightning rod in that battle, with critics accusing him of trafficking in conspiratorial anti-Israel rhetoric, while supporters view him challenging standard establishment thinking.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Cuba's healthcare system is facing mounting pressure as shortages of medicines, medical equipment, food and fuel disrupt hospital operations and leave
articles.body: Cuba's healthcare system is facing mounting pressure as shortages of medicines, medical equipment, food and fuel disrupt hospital operations and leave doctors struggling to provide essential treatment. The crisis has intensified amid renewed US sanctions and restrictions on supplies entering the Caribbean island, raising concerns over the impact of Washington's pressure campaign on ordinary Cubans.According to a report by CBS News' 60 Minutes, doctors at William Soler Pediatric Hospital in Havana are struggling to treat patients amid severe shortages of essential supplies.The report highlighted the case of a two-month-old malnourished baby who required specialised infant formula that was difficult to obtain. Doctors had to rely on locally available alternatives, including preparations made from malanga, a starchy root vegetable, and chicken.The baby later developed respiratory complications, was readmitted to the intensive care unit and died on Thursday, CBS News reported, citing the hospital's intensive care unit head, Dr Alejandro Chong.The situation reflects the growing strain on Cuba's healthcare system, where shortages of essential medicines and equipment are compounding the difficulties faced by doctors and patients.Dr Lórien Rodríguez, a second-year paediatric surgery resident, said the lack of resources was making their work increasingly difficult."There are fewer personnel, fewer resources, and it makes all the work we're doing much more difficult," she told CBS News, adding that doctors were often forced to tell patients they could not provide the treatment they needed.Cuba's deputy foreign minister Carlos Fernández de Cossío acknowledged that the government also had a role in addressing the crisis, despite blaming US restrictions for worsening the country's economic difficulties."Every government has responsibility for their people," he told CBS News, adding that the Cuban government had made decisions that could have been better.The healthcare crisis has been compounded by an acute energy shortage, with frequent power cuts disrupting hospital operations and putting patients dependent on life-support equipment at risk. Cuban doctors told CBS News that electricity failures had forced medical staff to complete surgeries using mobile phone flashlights. In some cases, when ventilators stopped working, doctors and nurses had to manually pump oxygen to keep patients alive.Cuban officials said the country had received only one oil tanker since early January, leaving it struggling to meet its fuel and electricity requirements.The US-Cuba conflict dates back to 1959, when Washington imposed economic restrictions following Fidel Castro's revolution. The Trump administration has intensified pressure on Havana in 2026, targeting its oil supplies and threatening tariffs on countries supplying fuel to the island.The pressure increased after the US capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, disrupting Cuba's access to a key oil supplier.You use AI every day. articles.title: Power outage hits Washington DC's Foggy Bottom, over 1,100 Pepco customers affected
articles.summary: More than 1,100 customers lost electricity in parts of Washington, DC, on Monday, November 2, after a power outage affected the Foggy Bottom and downtown
articles.body: More than 1,100 customers lost electricity in parts of Washington, DC, on Monday, November 2, after a power outage affected the Foggy Bottom and downtown areas, according to reports.The disruption affected 1,176 Pepco customers, with the outages concentrated in Foggy Bottom, an area that is home to the US State Department. Some affected locations were also a few blocks from the White House, the Wall Street Journal reported.Emergency crews responded after smoke was reported coming from multiple manholes. One incident was described as a manhole explosion directly in front of the World Bank building.Pepco said the probable cause of the outage was a failure at one of its substations. The utility was assessing the situation and had not provided a confirmed restoration timeline in the available reports.The outage came a day before Election Day, when voters across the country were preparing to cast their ballots in the midterm elections.DC power outage impacts GW University: DetailsPotomac Electric Power Company initially estimated power to be restored around 11 am. But officials later revised the estimated time to "pending assessment". The outage’s boundaries are currently unclear, as well as which buildings have fully lost power as inoperable traffic lights bring much of Foggy Bottom traffic to a crawl, with GW IT confirming the outage has impacted the Foggy Bottom Data Center and services like GWeb and classroom technology.GW Hatchet repored that officials have canceled all classes for the day, they shared in a GW Alert at 11:37 a.m. that all School of Medicine and Health Sciences and GW Law classes would continue in-person and remotely, along with operations on the University’s Arlington, Alexandria and Virginia Science and Technology campuses.A University spokesperson said the outage is affecting multiple GW campus buildings and the surrounding Foggy Bottom area, adding officials have canceled classes until noon and will provide a second update about classes later in the day before noon.Officials directed students encountering challenges entering their dorms to the key depot at 2025 F Street to pick up loaner keys.Other neighborhood buildings, including Western Market, the World Bank and International Monetary Fund appear to have also lost power.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jamal Edwards' sister on the 20-year legacy of SBTV
articles.summary: The online music platform helped launch the careers of acts like Dave, Ed Sheeran and Jessie J.
articles.body:
Launched in the early days of YouTube with homemade videos featuring emerging artists, online music channel SBTV went on to shake up the music industry.

Pioneering DJ and entrepreneur Jamal Edwards founded the grime and rap music platform back in 2006 after he got a camcorder for Christmas and started filming his friends on the council estate where he grew up in west London.

It helped launch the careers of many acts including Dave, Ed Sheeran, Jessie J and Skepta.

By the age of 23, Jamal was a multimillionaire and channelling his success into helping others. He was awarded an MBE for his services to music in 2014.

He died aged 31 in 2022 of cardiac arrhythmia following drug use, prompting a flood of tributes from those who he helped support.

As the channel marks its 20th anniversary, it is set to bring back some of its freestyle formats in the hope of discovering a new generation of rappers.

His sister has been keeping his legacy going by taking over as CEO of SBTV.

Tanisha, who is also a singer-songwriter and producer, feels in a world where algorithms influence what we listen to, it's important to still have platforms curated by music lovers.

"I know how it feels as an artist and trying to put yourself out there and break through those doors," she says.

"So I think it's very key to still have a platform that does want to help up-and-coming talent, that does want to go to places on the map that you wouldn't mainly really go to."

A host of the artists who were platformed on the channel, including Tinie Tempah, Lady Leshurr and Tinchy Stryder, are also set to perform at a one-off show held in London's O2 arena next week to mark the 20-year milestone.

The event, which will also see artists like Dappy, Headie One and Ms Banks take to the stage, will raise money for the Jamal Edwards Self Belief Trust.

Tanisha says being able to honour her brother's legacy "means everything".

"Obviously he's not physically here with us," she says.

"But to be able to carry on his name and carry on the work he did and be able to push his message of self-belief.

"And finding the next generation of talent, working with all these artists that he's previously worked with... I just feel really grateful, honoured and blessed that we're able to continue his name and legacy in such a way."

Rappers Nolay and Griminal are among those who see Jamal as a "catalyst" for their careers and say they're excited to celebrate his impact at the upcoming show.

Griminal recalls how the DJ had a "positive energy and spirit" and an eye for spotting "raw talent".

Nolay tells Newsbeat Jamal not only championed her work, but opened her eyes to the power of promoting your music online and creating a brand for yourself.

Boosting yourself on social media to break into the music industry has become a given in 2026 - something Nolay says has made things feel less "real".

"We're in a day and time where the connection's kind of being lost because of evolution and technology," Nolay says.

"But what happens is authenticity becomes lost along the way by doing that.

"And to have something like SBTV there and revert back to what Jamal was doing in the first place, it's gonna [be] such a large platform for artists that feel disheartened."

You can hear more about SBTV's legacy from the team's takeover on DJ Target's show on BBC Sounds.

articles.title: Accused arsonist in Los Angeles’ deadly Palisades fire returns for federal retrial
articles.summary: Jury selection began Monday in the federal retrial of a man prosecutors say deliberately set a blaze that grew into one of the deadliest, most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history.
articles.body: Jury selection began Monday in the federal retrial of a man prosecutors say deliberately set a blaze that grew into one of the deadliest, most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, whose initial three-week trial ended in a hung jury in late June, was slated to return to U.S. District Court in downtown Los Angeles to face a scaled-down version of the charges previously leveled against him. Rinderknecht, a former Uber driver of dual U.S.-French citizenship, was cast by prosecutors as a dejected loner who harbored deep anger at society, particularly the wealthy, and channeled his rage into an act of arson. He is accused of “maliciously” starting a brush fire on January 1, 2025, that was quickly extinguished but smoldered in the roots of dense scrub before re-igniting days later, whipped by fierce winds into a conflagration that laid waste to the seaside enclave of Pacific Palisades. Defense attorneys have maintained that Rinderknecht was wrongly accused. They asserted the hilltop New Year’s Day blaze was triggered by holiday fireworks, not their client, and that the massive Palisades inferno that killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes a week later was a separate fire set by someone else. The opposing narratives of the disaster left jurors deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquittal and unable to reach a unanimous verdict on any of the three charges in June. Judge Anne Hwang declared a mistrial, and prosecutors moved to retry the defendant under a grand jury indictment that dropped one of the original charges Rinderknecht faced and modified the two remaining federal arson counts. Nearly 7,000 homes and other structures went up in flames, with property losses estimated at $150 billion, some of that belonging to organizations receiving federal financial assistance or involved in interstate commerce. Simultaneous disasters The Palisades blaze coincided with another catastrophic wind-driven wildfire that erupted almost simultaneously in Eaton Canyon, about 30 miles to the east, killing 19 people and ravaging the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena. Fire investigators later concluded that sparks from an electrical transmission tower ignited the Eaton fire. Rinderknecht was the only person criminally charged in connection with either of the two January 7, 2025 blazes, which together rank as the deadliest wildfire calamity ever in Los Angeles County, surpassing the 29 lives lost in the Griffith Park fire of 1933. Rinderknecht, who pleaded not guilty, declined to testify in his own defense during his first trial. He would face up to 40 years in prison if found guilty as charged under the latest indictment. The original indictment carried a maximum prison term of 45 years. He has remained in custody since his arrest in Florida in October 2025. Defense attorney Steve Haney asserted during the first trial that prosecutors lacked physical evidence linking Rinderknecht to arson or any records showing an intent to commit arson. In court documents and public statements about the case, Haney also suggested that his client was being scapegoated for failures of the Los Angeles Fire Department. A onetime Pacific Palisades resident himself, Rinderknecht professed his innocence in a court declaration filed last March, denying he had willfully started any fire. He acknowledged witnessing the outbreak of the January 1, 2025 fire, originally called the Lachman fire, from the vantage point of a hill he had climbed to watch New Year’s fireworks. But Rinderknecht said he immediately called emergency 911 to report the blaze and remained at the scene until firefighters arrived and offered to help them. Prosecutors have alleged that while placing his 911 call, Rinderknecht asked the AI app ChatGPT on his phone whether someone could be found at fault for lighting a fire “because of your cigarettes,” to which ChatGPT replied, “Yes.” Prosecutors also said security camera footage and location data from Rinderknecht’s cellphone show he was the only person in the vicinity of the January 1 blaze when it began near a trail in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.

articles.title: Storms expected to hit parts of Texas and Kansas on Election Day
articles.summary: Soggy, dreary weather is expected to hit the central U.S. as voters head to the polls Tuesday, but experts said the impact on the electoral outcome is expected to be minimal.
articles.body: Soggy, dreary weather is expected to hit the central U.S. as voters head to the polls Tuesday, but experts said the impact on the electoral outcome is expected to be minimal. Still, weather could become a closely watched factor in a few tight races in Texas and the Midwest. On Monday, a storm system is expected to move through the central U.S., with hurricane-strength winds, the risk of tornadoes, hail and heavy rainfall. “We’ve got some moisture that’s moving up into parts of Texas and Oklahoma and up into Kansas and Missouri, and with that moisture, we’re going to have a chance of storms,” said Evan Bentley, the warning coordination meteorologist for the National Weather Service Storm Prediction Center in Norman, Oklahoma. “We have plenty of energy available to support severe weather, including damaging winds and perhaps a few tornadoes.” Bentley said North Texas and Oklahoma could see straight-line winds in excess of 75 mph on Monday, raising some concern about power outages. “There’s always concern, when we have the potential for winds of 70 to 80 miles per hour, of having impacts on infrastructure, such as power lines,” Bentley said, though he added that this type of weather was not uncommon in the region. The weather’s effect on voter turnout will be watched closely by campaigns seeking to draw as many supporters as possible to polling places. Kansas and Texas, which could both be affected by the storms Monday, have hotly contested Senate races. The storm system will move east Tuesday, with heavy rainfall possible in Mississippi, Missouri and western Tennessee. On Election Day, “scattered flash floods are possible” in the lower Mississippi River valley and into areas such as Memphis, said Jennifer Tate, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center in College Park, Maryland. Much of the rest of the central U.S. — from East Texas to the Midwest — can expect wet, dreary weather on Election Day. “There still could be some locally heavy amounts in Iowa,” Tate said of rainfall. “Hopefully not anything that would impact travel too much.” Election Day weather on the West Coast looks fairly pleasant, with pockets of rainfall in Northern California. The East Coast looks clear, also, with some rainfall expected in Florida and Maine. Rainfall has been shown to have a modest effect on voter turnout in analyses of voting data. Researchers have analyzed past elections for trends in how unusually heavy rainfall might have suppressed voter turnout in historical elections. Brad Gomez, an associate professor of political science at Florida State University, was part of a team that analyzed presidential elections from 1948 to 2000. “What we found was that for every inch of rain that a county received above its average amount of rainfall, voter turnout went down about eight-tenths of 1 percentage point,” Gomez said. But Gomez said there have been institutional changes in voting that make it hard to estimate whether that effect will carry through today. “Many states started to adopt early voting, and, of course, some states, like Washington and Oregon, started to adopt mail-in voting,” Gomez said. “Nationally, the U.S. Election Assistance Commission estimates that today only about 37% of Americans actually vote on Election Day.” That means weather disruptions affect a much smaller slice of voters now than they did before the year 2000. Early voting trends could mean weather disruptions are more impactful in some states than others. Gomez said only about 20% of Texans cast their ballots in person on Election Day in the 2024 election. But that number was about 60% in Minnesota and about 45% in Kansas — so weather disruptions could be more meaningful in those states. Thomas Fujiwara, an associate professor of economics at Princeton University who has studied the issue and written about it in academic papers, said the effect of rainfall on turnout has decreased over time. “It was stronger in the ’50s and ’60s, and it’s weaker now,” Fujiwara said. “We shouldn’t think of rain being a major driver.” Both Fujiwara and Gomez said it would be hard to predict which party stands to gain from rain, given the relatively recent changes to how people vote.

articles.title: In 1996, Paul McCartney helped open a performing arts institute in a former Liverpool school; 30 years later, the institution awarded its first degrees and celebrated over 400 graduates from 28 countries
articles.summary: Thirty years after Sir Paul McCartney helped open the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts (LIPA) in a former Liverpool school, the institution has
articles.body: Thirty years after Sir Paul McCartney helped open the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts (LIPA) in a former Liverpool school, the institution has reached a milestone that blends history with a new beginning. At its 2026 graduation ceremony, LIPA conferred its first LIPA degrees and celebrated more than 400 graduating students from 28 countries. The event, held on 21 July at the Liverpool Experience Campus, also honoured leading figures from film, theatre, music and arts management, with McCartney present as the institute’s Founding Patron. Read more details about it, as per LIPA's website, here:From a former school to LIPALIPA was founded by Sir Paul McCartney and Mark Featherstone-Witty and opened in 1996 in the former Liverpool Institute for Boys, the school McCartney once attended. The idea was to create a place where performers and the people who work behind the scenes could train together, reflecting the practical realities of the creative industries. That founding vision remains visible in the institute’s course structure. LIPA offers undergraduate, master’s and foundation certificate programmes in acting, dance, music, musical theatre, filmmaking, theatre production, design, sound technology and creative arts management. The aim is not only to develop individual talent, but to prepare students to collaborate across disciplines once they enter professional work.A milestone graduationThe 2026 ceremony was described by LIPA’s Principal and Chief Executive, Professor Sean McNamara, as a milestone graduation. As the institute marked its 30th anniversary, it also conferred its first LIPA degrees, giving the class of 2026 a place in the institution’s history. More than 400 students graduated, representing 28 countries including Colombia, Georgia, India, Mexico, Peru and Venezuela. McNamara said the graduates were leaving as artists, innovators and leaders, equipped with the skills, vision and confidence to shape the creative and cultural industries.McCartney honoured five creative leadersSir Paul McCartney awarded LIPA Companionships to five leading figures from the creative industries. The honour recognises outstanding achievement in the sector as well as a significant contribution to student learning.Among the recipients was Merseyside-born actor, writer and producer Stephen Graham, known for work including This Is England, Boardwalk Empire, Line of Duty, Boiling Point and Adolescence. Graham has received BAFTA, Primetime Emmy and Golden Globe recognition during a career that has made him one of Britain’s most respected screen actors.The other Companions were BAFTA-winning actor and writer Cathy Tyson; Paul Duhaney, artistic director of Africa Oyé; McFly founding member and Paddington: The Musical composer Tom Fletcher; and film producer Lynette Howell Taylor. Howell Taylor’s honour carried particular significance because she graduated from LIPA’s management degree in 2000 before building a career in Los Angeles, where she has produced more than 25 feature films, including 'A Star Is Born'. In 2025, she was elected president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.A full-circle momentFor Howell Taylor, the ceremony was a return to the place where her professional journey began. She said LIPA gave her the foundation for her career and was the first environment in which she felt truly seen for her passion and abilities. She credited its teachers with encouraging and challenging her to explore what she could achieve.She also thanked McCartney and Featherstone-Witty for creating a creative, cross-disciplinary environment where both artists and those who enable or work with artists can thrive. Her words captured the broader purpose of LIPA: to support not only performers, but producers, managers, technicians and designers who help bring creative work to audiences.Liverpool’s creative legacyThe institute’s growth reflects Liverpool’s continuing influence on British and international culture. From its roots in a former school associated with McCartney’s own youth, LIPA has become a training ground for students from around the world, with graduates entering music, theatre, film, television and the wider creative economy.The 2026 graduation showed how far that idea has travelled. A local institution built around collaboration has become a global community, with students from five continents celebrating together and industry leaders returning to recognise the next generation.Looking to the next 30 yearsAs LIPA enters its fourth decade, the first degree awards mark both an ending and a beginning. The class of 2026 leaves with qualifications bearing the institute’s name, while the wider LIPA community continues to develop talent across performance, production, design, technology and management.For McCartney, the ceremony was another chapter in a project that began with a simple ambition: to give young creative people the training, confidence and connections they need to build sustainable careers. Thirty years on, with more than 400 graduates from 28 countries celebrating together, that ambition is being carried forward by a new generation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
